chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, said:
Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) was handed over to Nahrir, and he used to constrain him and harm him.
He said: Then his wife said to him, "Woe to you! Be wary of Allah. You do not know who is in your house." And she informed him of his righteousness, and said, "Indeed, I fear for you because of him."
So he said, "I will surely throw him among the beasts of prey." Then he did that to him, and he (عليه السلام) was seen standing in salat (prayer) while they were around him.

key_terms.سُلِّمَ: was handed over or delivered into custody
key_terms.يُضَيِّقُ: was constraining, pressuring, or treating harshly

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the righteousness and divine protection of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This report recounts a trial faced by Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (عليه السلام), during which he was mistreated by his custodian. Despite this oppression, his spiritual rank became evident when he was seen standing in salat (prayer) unharmed among predatory beasts, reflecting his righteousness and divine protection.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from some of our companions who said,

‘Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) was submitted (for custody) to an animal keeper, and he<sup>asws</sup> was constricting upon him<sup>asws</sup> and was hurting him<sup>asws</sup>.

So his wife said to him, ‘Woe be unto you! Fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Do you not know who is in your house?’ And she introduced him<sup>asws</sup> of his<sup>asws</sup> righteousness and she said, ‘I fear upon you from him<sup>asws</sup>’.
So he said, ‘I shall throw himasws between the predatory animals’. Then he did that with himasws, and heasws was seen standing praying Salat and they were around himasws’.
en.sarwar: 25. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from certain persons of our people who have narrated the following. “

mmd ibn al-Hujr once wrote to abu Muhammad (a.s.) complaining against ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Dulf and Yazid ibn ‘Abdallah. He wrote back in reply, “As far as ‘Abd al-‘Aziz is concerned I have relieved you from his troubles. As far as Yazid is concerned for each of you there is position before Allah.” ‘Abd al-‘Aziz died and Yazid killed Muhammad ibn Hujr.”
